cells.tense: The repetition and the aim seem to be feeding each other right now.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Something in the routine stays only from old habit. Drop it, and carry the rest forward as it is.
cells.core:
The work you repeat has an aim, and the aim is yours. You start, you stop, you come back, and the coming back is what keeps the road under you. Nothing in it reads as a fight, and refining a piece doesn't turn into worrying at it. When the full version stops fitting the reason you keep it, you can set that version down and lose nothing that mattered.

The smallest part that is only there from habit: stop carrying it. What remains keeps the shape it had. If something in you still wants to hold that piece upright, let it fall anyway — a thing built to stand didn't need your arm.
cells.sheetLine: Your practice is aimed somewhere, and it can breathe while it aims.
cells.verb: keep at the same thing until the skill has moved into your hands
cells.place: in drive — on the way toward what you are building, moving to arrive

cells.tense: From where you stand, the practice will be tightened again before the last round is through.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Set down the piece you keep reworking. Leave it standing as it is, and don't fill the gap.
cells.core:
The polishing has outrun the work. You keep smoothing a piece — a form, a plan, one detail — that was already good enough, and no session lands as finished because you are already living inside the next version of it. That is what is eating the hours that used to belong to the doing. The bar moves as you clear it.

Set one piece down. The one you keep reworking: leave it exactly as it stands, and don't fill the space with extra sessions. A week away from it will tell you more than another pass would. What holds will still be there; what doesn't was only held up by your arm.
cells.sheetLine: The fine-tuning has quietly become the grip you can't release.

cells.tense: The repetitions stopped long before the skill had a chance to settle.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Sit down with the work once, short and unglamorous, stop on purpose, then take the evening back.
cells.core:
Starting and stopping taught something else: that a stretch of effort ends with a door shutting. So you have quit sitting down with anything for long. The skill is missing, and so is the memory of what it was for. The destination is still real. What is gone is the proof you used to have that you can build toward it without the floor tilting.

Give the work a small amount of time — shorter than feels serious, kept, nothing demanded of it — and finish on purpose rather than by running out. Close it out loud once, so your hands learn the difference between done and dropped. Then take the evening back, owed and unspent.
cells.sheetLine: Showing up stopped feeling safe before it stopped being possible.

cells.tense: The practice is running, and your account of yourself lags behind it.
cells.act: picture it a year on, turned out well, and keep the picture
cells.ask: Sketch where this lands a year from now, going right, on one page. No plan, nobody shown.
cells.core:
You can already do the thing — the hands know the rounds, the body carries the skill — but when someone asks what you are working on, the answer comes out as keeping busy or being between things. The doing has an aim. The saying has none. Where you are pointed is real; only the telling of it is blank.

Sketch it. Where this ends up a year from now if it goes right: one page, a few strokes, no plan attached, no explanation owed to anyone. Badly is fine. It doesn't have to be accurate, and nobody has to see it. A thing drawn is a thing you have stopped hiding from yourself.
